newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Economic output excluding agriculture is crawling along at a pace far short of the growth rate necessary to meet the country's need to create jobs, economists said. Latest figures show growth in gross domestic product (GDP) slowed to 3.2 percent in the third quarter from a revised 3.7 percent in the second.

- Taiwan issued a formal protest over South Africa's decision to drop its diplomatic recognition in favour of Beijing, saying official aid projects would be reviewed, but trade ties were unlikely to affected severely.
- The government mining engineer is to investigate the mudslide disaster at Vancouver-listed Botswana Diamondfields Inc's Rovic diamond mine in which up to 22 miners are believed to have died.

- Petrol and diesel prices are likely to rise sharply from next Wednesday as the higher international price trends of recent months, along with the weaker rand, continue to work their way into the pricing system.

- Land Affairs and Agirculture Minister Derek Hanekom abolished maize floor prices and price stabilisation for farmers, plunging the industry into a free market and provoking mixed reaction from the sector.

- Conservative Freedom Front leader Constand Viljoen revealed that the right wing had had plans to establish an Afrikaner state by military means, months before South Africa's first all-race elections in April 1994.

- Sentrachem, one of South Africa's largest chemical groups, shed 630 million rand in value on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange after an announcement that its Senachem subsidiary had incurred substantial forward foreign exchange losses.

- Officials of Botswana Diamondfields Inc are expected in South Africa within days to assess the mine disaster at the Rovic mine in the Free State province. The National Union of Mineworkers alleged that risk assessment procedures at the mine were neglected and rescue operations delayed.

- Commercial and development rights to four of Mpumalanga's flagship wildlife parks have been sold to Dubai-based Dolphin Group for 50 years, in a controversial deal to bankroll the province's parks board.
- Stronger-than-expected figures for GDP growth in the third quarter have forced economists to revise their forecasts upwards for economic growth over the full year.
- The death toll in the Rovic diamond mine disaster in the Free State is expected to reach 22 after the search for 18 miners still trapped underground was called off because of heavy rains.
